title: locallibrary-plugin.toml
description: A locallibrary plugin's manifest as its author writes it: who the plugin is, what it may call back for and what it adds. Keys it doesn't list are allowed, so an older locallibrary reads a newer plugin's manifest. `Manifest::validate` in loclib-plugin checks the rest: names, versions, schemas that compile and what needs a capability.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter.

protocol.description: The protocol versions it speaks, as a semver requirement (`^0.2`).

capabilities.description: What it may call back for (see [`Capability`]).

accounts.description: The account types it asks for, and the scopes of each it needs.

net.description: How often the host may send `net/fetch` requests to some of the hosts it talks to.

AccountNeed.description:
`[[accounts]]`: an account type a plugin asks for, the scopes of it it needs and why, and those
it can do without.

type.description: The account type (`google`), which an account plugin provides.

scopes.description: The type's scopes it needs, by name (`youtube-upload`).

why.description: Why it needs them, shown when the user gives it access.

optional.description: Scopes it asks for besides, which the user may leave out.

OptionalScopes.description:
`optional = [{ scopes = ["read"], why = "..." }]`: scopes a plugin can do without, and what
they're for.

AccountType.description:
`[[contributes.account_types]]`: an account type, signed in to in the browser, or by entering
keys (`kind = "keys"`). Its OAuth fields are an account type's signed in to in the browser,
and only its; `keys`, `keys_url` and `authorization` are one's signed in to with keys, and only
its.

type.description: The account type it provides (`google`), which other account plugins may provide too.

kind.description: How it's signed in to: in the browser unless it says.

authorize_url.description: The service's authorization endpoint, where the browser signs in (https).

token_url.description:
Its token endpoint, where the host trades the browser's code for tokens and refreshes
them (https). An account type signed in to in the browser has this or `token_exchange`.

token_exchange.description:
Local Network's token exchange for its service, in `token_url`'s place: only in an
account plugin locallibrary ships, since it signs people in as Local Network.

client_id.description:
Its client at the service: a public one, without a secret, or Local Network's, whose
secret the token exchange holds.

revoke_url.description: Where its tokens are revoked at signing out (RFC 7009), when the service has one (https).

token.description: Where its access token goes in a request: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` unless it says.

redirect_port.description:
The port on 127.0.0.1 the browser comes back to, for a service that compares the redirect
URI with the one its client was registered with. Any free port otherwise.

always.description: The service's scopes every sign-in asks for, as the service names them (`openid`).

whoami.description:
Where the host asks the service who signed in. One signed in to with keys may leave it
out: the user names the account then.

one_account.description:
The authorize params that sign in again as one account the host knows (`login_hint =
"{subject}"`): their values may name it only as [`SUBJECT_PLACEHOLDER`].

another_account.description:
The authorize params that sign in to another account than those the browser has
(`prompt = "select_account"`).

params.description:
The authorize params every sign-in sends besides (`access_type = "offline"`), none of
`one_account`'s or `another_account`'s.

keys.description: The keys the user enters, by name (`access`), which the service gave them.

authorization.description:
The `Authorization` header's value they make in a request (`LOW {access}:{secret}`), each
key named in braces.

scopes.description: What a plugin may be given access to, by name (`youtube-upload`).

SignIn.description: How an account of a type is signed in to.

oneOf.description: In the browser, with OAuth 2: `oauth`.
By entering the keys the service gave the user: `keys`.

TokenPlace.description:
Where an account type's access token goes in a `net/fetch` request: `token = { scheme =
"OAuth" }` or `token = { query = "access_token" }`. The request names the account there, and
only there.

oneOf.description: The `Authorization` header, as this scheme and the token (`OAuth <token>`).

This query parameter's value (`?access_token=<token>`), for a service that takes it only
there (Mixcloud).

Whoami.description:
`whoami = { url = "...", subject = "/sub", name = "/email" }`: the endpoint the host gets with a
new access token, or keys just entered, and JSON pointers into its answer.

subject.description: The account's id at the service, which tells two accounts apart (`/sub`).

name.description: What the account is shown as (`/email`).

title.description: What it's called where the user gets it (`S3 access key`).

Scope.description: `[contributes.account_types.scopes.<name>]`: one thing a plugin may do with an account.

asks.description:
The service's scopes it asks for at signing in, as the service names them. None for a
scope only locallibrary knows, which the service's own scopes already allow.

requests.description: The requests it covers: the only ones the host fills the account's token into for it.

ScopeRequest.description:
`{ method = "POST", url = "https://www.googleapis.com/upload/youtube/v3/videos*" }`: requests
with this method to this URL, or to any URL starting with it when it ends in `*`. The URL is
written as it's read (`https://a.com/*`, not `https://a.com*`), so the start it names is a whole
host.

plan.description:
Planned first: the host asks for a dry run, shows its plan ([`CommandPlan`]) and runs it
only once the user confirms.

long_running.description:
Running it takes a while: hosts show its progress and offer to stop it, and give it longer
to stop once asked before they kill the plugin.

params.description: A JSON Schema for its params (an object).

cli.description: Its own place on the command line (see [`Operation::cli`]).

oneOf.description: Answers any JSON, shown as it is (`--json`) or not at all.
Answers a [`crate::View`].

Where.description:
Where a host offers a command or an operation: in the menu of the tracks selected, of a
playlist, or of a drive; or, for a command alone, with what's about rekordbox's collection on
this computer rather than a drive (`collection`). A host's palette has every one.

oneOf.description:
About this computer's rekordbox collection, not a track, a playlist or a drive: run without
one (a backup of the collection, say). Commands only: an operation edits a drive.

Destination.description:
`[[contributes.destinations]]`: somewhere the user copies their store to (`store`), or
publishes sets at (`set`).

oneOf.description: Copies of the store: `blobs/*` and `manifest/*`.
Sets, published: `set/publish`.

Listener.description: `[[contributes.events]]`: what the plugin is told of (`event/notify`).

EventName.description:
What a host tells plugins of: a closed list, each needing a capability (see
[`EventName::capability`]).

oneOf.description: A drive was plugged in.
A drive was unplugged.
A drive's databases or its locallibrary state changed (`payload.changed` says which).

A drive was saved into the store as a new snapshot (`payload.history_lists`: the
history lists the store lacked).
A drive back from a set was saved beside its library's newest snapshot.
A request to the sidecar finished (`payload.method`, `payload.ok`).
A plan was applied (`payload.operation`, `payload.summary`).

Operation.description:
Planned with `op/plan`, applied by the host, which works out from the edits whether it's
destructive.

long_running.description: Planning takes a while: the host shows progress.

params.description: A JSON Schema for its params (an object).

cli.description:
Its own place on the command line, rather than `locallibrary <plugin> <name>`: a
top-level command (`import`), or one in a group of the host's (`playlist import`).
Built-in plugins only.

Panel.description:
Shown under a track's details, as `panel/render` answers for the track. Hosts ask for it as
the user comes to a track, so it answers quickly, reading only what it needs.

where.description: What it's shown with: a track, unless it says.

Analyzer.description: Run with `track/analyze`; its fields become columns.

version.description:
Its own version: the host keeps its values by it, so a new one works them out again. Bump
it whenever the values would change.

roles.description:
Which of its fields has each role it answers (`bpm = "bpm"`): what the host reads for
that role (see [`Role`]).

display.description:
How hosts show some of its fields, by field (`display.lufs = { unit = "LUFS" }`): in the
player's columns, `track show` and the mix report.

oneOf.description: A beat grid (feature `analysis`, see [`crate::Output`]).
A song structure: the mood and the phrases (feature `analysis`).
A waveform in three bands, in a blob (feature `analysis`).

FieldDisplay.description:
How hosts show a field's values, each part optional. Without them a number shows to two
places at most (trailing zeros left out), a list joined with commas, a boolean as yes or no.

unit.description: Said after a value (`LUFS`); a `db` format's is `dB` unless it says.

width.description: How wide its column is in the player, in cells (1 to 40); for a `meter`, how long it is.

FieldFormat.description: What a field's values are, for hosts to show them as such.

oneOf.description: A key (a string), as the host shows keys.
Seconds (a number), as minutes and seconds (`3:07`, `1:02:03`).
Decibels (a number), signed (`+0.4 dB`, `-8.2 dB`).
A fraction (a number, 0 to 1) as a percentage (`85%`; no decimal places unless it says).
A fraction (a number, 0 to 1) as a bar, `width` cells long (8 unless it says).

Check.description:
Run with `check/run` on a drive along with locallibrary's own checks, and with `plan/check`
before a plan is applied: as its `when` says.

default_on.description: It runs unless the user turns it off; otherwise, once they turn it on.

when.description:
When it runs: with the check before a set and doctor (`check`, the default), and before a
plan is applied (`apply`: a guard).

oneOf.description: With locallibrary's check before a set and doctor (`check/run`).
Before a plan is applied (`plan/check`): a guard.

extension.description:
The file it writes ends in this: lowercase letters and digits, without the dot (`nml`).
Either this or `folder`.

options.description: A JSON Schema for its options (an object).

source.description:
What it writes out [default: a drive's library]: one source (`"set"`), or a list of them
(`["drive", "set", "mix"]`) for an exporter that writes each out the same way.

ExportSources.description: What an exporter writes out, as its manifest says it: one source, or a list.

oneOf.description: A drive's library.
A set the DJ declared (`locallibrary sets`).
A recorded mix's tracklist, as `locallibrary mix` found it.

Importer.description:
Run with `import/read` on a file the user names: the host finds what it read on a drive and
plans the edits itself, so it needs no capability to plan one.

extension.description:
The file it reads usually ends in this: lowercase letters and digits, without the dot
(`nml`).

options.description: A JSON Schema for its options (an object).

provides.description: What it reads: what of a track's (and the plays) the host takes from it.

oneOf.description: A track's key and BPM.
My Tags.
What played, as sessions.

Provider.description:
Asked with `provide/candidates` for what it has for tracks, of its kind: the host offers the
user every provider's, and makes the edits chosen itself. It's given the tracks' tags, which
takes `library:read`, and needs no capability to plan an edit.

ProviderKind.description: What a provider finds for a track.

oneOf.description: Cover art: an image.
Tags: a title, an artist, an album...

Service.description:
Started with `service/start` by a host that stays open (the player, the sidecar, the `watch`
agent), once the user has turned it on (its plugin's setting `services.<name>`), never by a
command run once.

LibrarySource.description:
Read with `library/read`, a page at a time, for the host to build a drive from. It's given the
folders the user grants it, which takes `fs:read`.

options.description: A JSON Schema for its options (an object).

Theme.description:
`[[contributes.themes]]`: a theme's colours, by the names of [`theme::TOKENS`] as tables (`cues.hot =
"#28e214"`, `ui = { accent = "#ff8800" }`), each `#rrggbb` (a gradient, `waveform.*`, a list
of two or more). What it leaves out is the default's.

Setting.description: A setting the host stores and shows in its settings.

oneOf.description: One of `choices`.

A password or a key: kept in the system's keychain, never shown, and given to the plugin
only as the host fills it into its `net/fetch` requests. It has no default.

NetLimit.description:
`[[net]]`: at most `per_second` `net/fetch` requests a second to `host`, one of the plugin's
`net:` capabilities as it's written (`musicbrainz.org`, `*.archive.org`), however many hooks
are under way: the limit the server asks its clients to keep.
